citations.title: Home Health, Home Services, and Home Nursing Agency Licensing Act
citations.requirement: No one may open, manage, conduct or maintain a home services agency without an IDPH license. The Act is the enabling statute for 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245. (From the fact-checked research; Act text not re-fetched.)

citations.title: Home Health, Home Services, and Home Nursing Agency Code
citations.requirement: Part 245 has four subparts: A General (245.10-245.25), B Operational Requirements (245.30-245.75), C Licensure Procedures (245.80-245.150), D Client/Patient Services (245.200-245.250). Section titles were confirmed from the table of contents. Most recent amendment shown: 49 Ill. Reg. 4661, eff. 3/25/2025.

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: Programs serving clients exclusively through IDoA CCP, DHS Office of Rehabilitation Services, or the VA are not home services agencies. 'Client record' means personal information, emergency notification information, agreed service plans, the home services contract, and documentation of services at each visit.

citations.title: Organization and Administration - Governing Body (all agencies)
citations.requirement: The agency must have a governing body with legal authority. The body must have bylaws or the equivalent, reviewed annually and revised as needed, that state the agency's objectives. It must adopt and revise operating policies and procedures, meet to review agency operations, and keep minutes of all meetings. The requirement to employ a qualified administrator is for home health agencies.

citations.title: Administration - all agencies
citations.requirement: The agency needs written administrative policies and procedures to ensure safe and adequate care. It must show evidence of liability insurance per 245.90(a). It must have written complaint-resolution policies between the agency and its clients and client advocates.

citations.title: Personnel policies - all agencies
citations.requirement: Written personnel policies must cover: (A) wage scales, benefits, hours and leave; (B) initial health evaluation of each new employee with client contact; (C) orientation and continuing education; (D) job descriptions for all positions; (E) annual performance evaluation; (F) Civil Rights Act of 1964 compliance; (G) confidentiality of personnel records; (H) employee health policy, including symptom and exposure reporting and removal from and return to client contact; (I) procedures for identifying and protecting staff from dangers in the home.

citations.title: Personnel - license verification, personnel records, contracted staff
citations.requirement: Before employing anyone in a position needing a State professional license, verify with IDFPR that the license is active and keep a copy in the personnel file. Personnel records must hold name and address, SSN, date of birth, next of kin, evidence of qualifications, employment dates, and the reason for separation. Home services agencies that use contracted services must ensure those workers hold any required license, registration or certification and are supervised by the agency.

citations.title: Agency Manager - Home Services and Home Nursing Agencies
citations.requirement: A home services agency must designate a person to supervise the provision of services (or oversee placement of workers). This is the verified designation rule. The research's reference to '245.40(f)' could not be confirmed and should not be used. No manager qualification list for home services agencies appears in 245.30(f) as fetched.

citations.title: Staffing - Administrator or Agency Manager responsibilities
citations.requirement: The manager must ensure legal compliance, know the Department's rules, keep them in the agency, and familiarize employees with the Act and rules. The manager keeps reports, records, personnel files and policies, maintains an organizational chart, hires per job descriptions, and provides orientation and in-service education. The manager must designate in writing a qualified person to act in the manager's absence. The agency must keep an office with a working telephone staffed during business hours. The office must protect record confidentiality and comply with fire-safety ordinances. The agency must adopt a written operating-hours policy that tells clients how to access care outside those hours.

citations.title: Home Services or In-Home Services Worker - definition and duties
citations.requirement: Home services means help with ADLs, housekeeping, personal laundry and companionship in the client's residence. It excludes anything requiring a Nurse Practice Act licensee. Workers may observe and report changes in client functioning, do chores and meal preparation, help with shopping and appointments, provide companionship, document services, and assist with ADLs and personal care. Workers provide services only as Part 245 allows.

citations.title: Acceptable tasks and limitations (skin care through toileting)
citations.requirement: Task-by-task limits apply for skin care, ambulation, bathing, dressing/compression, exercise, feeding/thickener, hair care, mouth care, nail care, positioning, shaving and toileting. Most require three things: client or representative feedback, worker training in the method, and an agency competency evaluation. Several also require a health care professional's order. No passive range of motion, no nail trimming, and no skilled skin care. The fetched page was truncated after toileting (L), so the remaining items (M-P) must be read in full.

citations.title: Medication reminding; prohibited medication setup
citations.requirement: A worker may remind a client about medications only when they were pre-selected by the client, a family member, a nurse or a pharmacist and are in containers other than prescription bottles, such as medication minders. A worker may not perform or provide medication setup. Source: ilga.gov excerpts and the Illinois Register adoption text, seen in search results. Confirm the exact subsection wording in the full text.

citations.title: Supervision of a home services worker
citations.requirement: A supervisor must be designated and available to workers for questions at all times (not applicable to placement agencies). Supervisory visits must include an on-site visit within the next supervisory visit when an area of concern is noted. The supervisor must also make an annual on-site visit to observe and assess each worker giving care. The visit interval for routine supervision is not confirmed. A secondary source says 90 days; read the full text of (c)(6)(B) before publishing.

citations.title: Qualifications and Requirements for Home Services Workers - employment conditions
citations.requirement: For each worker who is not otherwise licensed, certified or registered, the agency must keep in the employee file documentation of: (1) no disqualifying Health Care Worker Background Check without a waiver; (2) a copy of the Social Security card; (3) a visa or proof of citizenship that meets federal employment requirements.

citations.title: Initial training - home services agency
citations.requirement: The agency must provide or arrange at least 10 hours of initial training per worker. Five hours must come before the first assignment, and the other 5 within 30 days of the start of employment. The agency may accept proof of training from another licensed home services agency within the prior 365 days, including a CNA on the Health Care Worker Registry. Such workers still get a competency evaluation before their first assignment. No assignment may be given until the worker passes a competency evaluation on the first 5 hours of topics, with a second test after the remaining 5 hours. (The 8-hour figure in 245.71(b) and 245.214(e) applies only to placement agencies.)

citations.title: Required training subjects
citations.requirement: Training must cover, in addition to 245.40(c)(4)(A)-(P): job responsibilities and limits; communication with people who are hard of hearing or have dementia; observing, reporting and documenting; personal care tasks including medication reminding; adaptive equipment; hygiene and infection control; a clean and safe environment; safety precautions; emergencies, first aid and the client's emergency preparedness plan; confidentiality; understanding dementia; problem-solving for challenging dementia behaviors; abuse and neglect and reporting duties; and any other task the agency assigns.

citations.title: Annual training
citations.requirement: Every worker needs at least 10 hours of training per year of employment, on a calendar-year or anniversary basis chosen by the agency. The initial 10 hours satisfy the first year. Self-study with demonstrated learning is allowed. Annual training must include: client dignity, independence, self-determination, privacy, choice and rights; disaster procedures; hygiene and infection control; abuse and neglect prevention and reporting; and the ADL tasks in 245.40(c)(4)(A)-(P), including oxygen delivery for workers who serve clients on oxygen.

citations.title: Supervisors/trainers and training documentation
citations.requirement: The agency must have home services supervisors or trainers who give initial training and ongoing supervision. Each must either (1) have at least 2 years of qualifying experience within the last 5 years, or (2) hold a current supervisory or trainer position and have had training within the past year on the permitted tasks, provided by or developed by a qualified professional. Supervisors and trainers must be available to workers for continuing education. All training must be documented with date, minutes per topic, instructor and qualifications, content description, and worker signature or electronic certificate with date/time stamp.

citations.title: Health Care Worker Background Check
citations.requirement: An agency must comply with the Health Care Worker Background Check Act (225 ILCS 46) and the Health Care Worker Background Check Code (77 Ill. Adm. Code 955).

citations.title: Health Care Worker Background Check Act and Code
citations.requirement: Fingerprint-based checks are required for covered workers. Fingerprints are sent to the Illinois State Police within 10 working days (per the research). Results initiated through IDPH are entered in the Health Care Worker Registry. The application package requires proof of access to the IDPH Registry (955.115, per Form 445104).

citations.title: Infection Control
citations.requirement: Each agency must develop and implement policies and procedures for investigating, controlling and preventing infections. The requirement for placement agencies to give workers the CDC hand-hygiene guideline does not apply to a direct-service agency. Subsection (b), on adherence to CDC guidance, was only partly visible; read it in full.

citations.title: Vaccinations (scope)
citations.requirement: Influenza and pneumococcal vaccination duties apply to home health agencies and home nursing agencies, not to home services agencies. Do not write client vaccination procedures for this license.

citations.title: Services - Home Services Agencies: scope and contracted services
citations.requirement: A home services agency provides non-medical services, directly or by contract, such as ADL support, personal care, medication reminding, housekeeping, laundry, cooking, shopping, transport to appointments, household records and companionship. The agency must keep a list of services offered and the scope of work for each. It must give that list to clients before contracting, with the signed contract, and whenever it changes. Contracts with third-party providers must be written and include 9 elements: services, adherence to agency policies and personnel requirements, agency control, notes, charges, liability and insurance, term, signatures, and termination.

citations.title: Written client agreement
citations.requirement: A written client agreement must include: (1) assurance of compliance with the Act, including the Health Care Worker Background Check Act; (2) who pays employment taxes, Social Security taxes and workers' compensation; (3) who supervises workers and who hires, fires and disciplines them; (4) charges, payment schedule and payee; (5) contract term and termination conditions; (6) contact information for concerns, complaints and questions.

citations.title: Acceptance of clients; discharge
citations.requirement: The agency must develop and follow written acceptance and discharge policies. Acceptance is based on need for non-medical help, and the agency may not provide medical services. A totally dependent repositioning client may be accepted only if the worker is trained and competency-evaluated and the representative can assist or give feedback. No one may be refused service on the basis of the protected classes listed in 775 ILCS 5/1-103(Q). Termination requires at least 7 working days' written notice with a stated reason, kept in the record. The 7-day notice does not apply when worker safety is at risk, and the risk must be documented. Acceptance must be based on documented functional limitations and relevant circumstances, including basic information on medications, treatments, activity, diet and mental status.

citations.title: Service plan
citations.requirement: A plan is required for every client, developed with agency staff, the client or representative or POA, and family if the client wishes. It must cover ADL and in-home support, medication reminders (frequency and time of day), treatments being received, activity, diet, functional limitations and essential procedures, mental health status, frequency of visits, equipment, and client limitations. It may not include tasks outside the worker scope in 245.40(c)(4). No physician signature is required. Review and revise as needed, and at least annually.

citations.title: Client records, retention, confidentiality
citations.requirement: Each client record must hold identifying information, representative contact information, an emergency contact, the agreed service plan, the signed home care services agreement, and worker documentation of each service at each visit. A written records policy is required. Records must be kept at least 2 years after the last date of service, in hard copy or electronic form. Faxed copies must be on non-thermal paper. A written confidentiality policy must cover use, removal and release of records.

citations.title: Services - Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias
citations.requirement: The section exists per the table of contents. Its text was not retrieved. IDPH's FAQ points agencies to 77 Ill. Adm. Code 973 for dementia requirements. Read both before finalizing the dementia policy.

citations.title: Staff Training (Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias Code)
citations.requirement: IDPH survey guidance names this section as the training standard for home services and home nursing agencies, together with 245.71. The rule text and dementia hour counts were not retrieved. A secondary source says 6 hours initial and 3 hours annual; treat that as unverified.

citations.title: Client Service Contracts - Home Nursing and Home Services Agencies
citations.requirement: The section title was confirmed from the table of contents. Its text was not retrieved. Use the 245.210(c) contract elements above, then read 245.220 in full for added contract terms.

citations.title: Quality Improvement Program
citations.requirement: Home nursing, home services and placement agencies must develop a quality improvement program with written policies. The program must evaluate the agency's total program at least once a year. Subsection (b) requires record review. Its detail, and the content of the evaluation for home services agencies, was not retrieved; read in full.

citations.title: Abuse, Neglect and Financial Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
citations.requirement: On reasonable suspicion of abuse, neglect or financial exploitation of a client aged 60+, a disabled client, or any 'eligible adult' under the Adult Protective Services Act (320 ILCS 20), notify the elder abuse provider agency designated by IDoA or the Area Agency on Aging. For a victim under 18, call the DCFS Child Abuse Hotline. Document each report and keep it on premises for 12 months. If an employee is the alleged perpetrator, remove them from direct client contact immediately and investigate. Complete a written investigation report within 14 days of the initial report. Send it to IDPH within 24 hours after the investigation is completed and keep a copy for 12 months. The report must contain the six elements in (d). Employees and volunteers must report to management and to the elder abuse provider agency or IDoA. Call 911 or local police immediately for staff-inflicted physical injury, sexual abuse by staff, a crime in the home by another person, or a death other than by disease or natural causes. A written law-enforcement notification policy is required. Mandated-reporter duties under 320 ILCS 20 remain.

citations.title: Services - Home Services Placement Agency
citations.requirement: A placement agency may not be the employer, may not direct or supervise the worker, and may charge only a one-time placement fee. It must identify itself as a placement agency in all marketing. This section does not apply to a direct-service (employer) agency; the manual should state which model the agency uses.

citations.title: License Application - evidence of liability insurance
citations.requirement: The agency must show evidence of liability insurance. The 245.30(b)(2) text confirms the cross-reference. The minimum limits were not confirmed; a secondary source says $1M per occurrence and $3M aggregate, which is unverified.

citations.title: Provisional License
citations.requirement: Provisional license valid 240 days, extendable 120 days with substantial progress. The full home services license expires one year from the end of the month the provisional license was first issued. (From the fact-checked research.)

citations.title: Adverse Licensure Actions - application not completed within 90 days
citations.requirement: An application not completed and approved within 90 days of submission may be denied (as cited by IDPH; from the research).

citations.title: Inspections and Investigations
citations.requirement: The section title was confirmed from the table of contents. Its text was not retrieved. Read it before writing the survey policy.

citations.title: Complaints
citations.requirement: The section title was confirmed from the table of contents. Its text was not retrieved. Read it before writing the IDPH-complaint procedure.

citations.title: Home Services Agencies Frequently Asked Questions
citations.requirement: Licensees take private pay or private insurance. Medicaid clients are served through IDoA CCP or DHS-DRS. IDPH does an initial application review within 30 days. A compliance survey takes place within 30 days of provisional license expiration. The agency needs IDPH approval before serving a new county. The agency must notify IDPH within 10 days of any change, using the Facility Information Change Form. (From the research.)

citations.cite: IDPH Guidance for Common Deficiency Findings
citations.title: Common Survey Deficiencies - annual registry verification and education
citations.requirement: Surveyors cite 245.71 (home services only) and 973.140 for training deficiencies. The guidance covers annual Health Care Worker Registry verification and annual education. Training records must show date, minutes per topic, instructor and qualifications, content and worker signature. This is survey guidance, not a rule.

citations.title: Home Services Application
citations.requirement: The application requires: complaint-resolution policy; employee health and safety policy; infection control policy; background-check process; supervisory-visit policies; employee training procedure (245.71); sample service plan; job descriptions; and proof of IDPH Registry access. A $1,500 fee by check or money order is due with the application. The form has an 'Alternate Agency Manager' line. (From the research.)

citations.cite: HFS Electronic Visit Verification; December 2025 Illinois EVV Updates
citations.title: Illinois EVV for Medicaid personal care
citations.requirement: Personal care and home health EVV data is integrated in HHAeXchange from March 2, 2026. HFS requires at least 75% quarterly EVV compliance from April 1, 2026. The state EVV solution is free to providers. (From the research.)

citations.cite: IDoA Community Care Program current rates (eff. 1/1/2026)
citations.title: CCP in-home service rate S5130
citations.requirement: CCP in-home service (S5130) is $30.80/hour statewide, or $32.57/hour with insurance. IDoA is the operating agency, and Care Coordination Units assess and refer clients. Senior HelpLine 1-800-252-8966 is for client applications. (From the research.)

citations.title: HSP maximum unit prices
citations.requirement: Homemaker (4100) $30.80/hour; personal assistant (4150) $20.00/hour; non-agency CNA (4198) $23.00/hour. HSP serves people with severe disabilities under age 60. (From the research.)

citations.cite: HFS Persons who are Elderly waiver
citations.title: Persons who are Elderly HCBS waiver
citations.requirement: HFS is the state Medicaid agency and IDoA is the operating agency for the Persons who are Elderly waiver. (From the research.)

citations.title: Illinois Minimum Wage Law
citations.requirement: State minimum wage law. Rates are from secondary sources and conflict for Chicago, so confirm with IDOL and the City of Chicago. Statute text was not retrieved. The URL is a placeholder; replace with the ilga.gov page for 820 ILCS 105.

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body and Agency Manager Responsibilities
state_specifics: Governing body holds legal authority. Bylaws or equivalent are reviewed annually, and the body keeps minutes of every meeting (245.30(a)).
The agency designates a person to supervise services (245.30(f)(1)). Do not cite 245.40(f) for this.
The manager must designate in writing a qualified person to act in the manager's absence (245.40(a)).
Keep an organizational chart and a copy of the Act and Part 245 on site (245.40(a)).
State in the manual that the agency is a direct-service (employer) agency, not a placement agency.

policies.title: Licensure, Service Area and Advertising Requirements
state_specifics: No one may open or operate a home services agency without an IDPH license (210 ILCS 55).
The $1,500 fee, paid by check or money order, is due with Form 445104. It is non-refundable.
Provisional license: 240 days, extendable 120 days. Full license expires one year from the end of the month the provisional license was first issued (245.100).
IDPH must approve each new county before the agency accepts clients there.
Advertise only as a licensed home services agency. The placement-agency identification rule (245.214) does not apply to a direct-service agency.

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control
state_specifics: The governing body adopts and revises operating policies and procedures (245.30(a)).
Bylaws are reviewed annually. Review the manual at least annually and record each revision date and approver in the governing body minutes.
Keep written administrative policies that ensure safe and adequate care (245.30(b)).

policies.title: Quality Improvement Program
state_specifics: Written quality improvement program required for home services agencies (245.240(a)).
Evaluate the agency's total program at least once a year.
Record review is required under 245.240(b). Read the full text for its detail.
Inputs to review: complaints, incidents, missed visits, supervisory visit findings, training completion.

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
state_specifics: The licensee serves private pay or private insurance clients. Medicaid clients are served through IDoA CCP or DHS-DRS.
Bill only for visits actually delivered and documented. Match EVV records to claims for any Medicaid-funded service.
Use CCP rate S5130 ($30.80/hour, or $32.57 with insurance) and the HSP unit prices only for authorized services.
Set up a confidential way for employees to report billing concerns.

policies.title: IDPH Surveys, Inspections and Complaint Investigations
state_specifics: IDPH conducts an on-site compliance survey within 30 days of the provisional license expiring.
Name one person to receive IDPH contacts and respond the same day.
Surveyors check training records, annual Registry verification and annual education (IDPH deficiency guidance).
Text of 245.110 and 245.115 was not retrieved. Read both in full before finalizing the procedure.

policies.title: Notification of Changes to IDPH and New-County Approval
state_specifics: Notify IDPH within 10 days of any change (ownership, manager, address, phone), using the Facility Information Change Form.
Get written IDPH approval before serving clients in a new county.
Renewal is due before the full license expires. Form 445104 says 60 days before expiration, so calendar a 90-day reminder.
Assign these deadlines to one named person.

policies.title: Office, Operating Hours and After-Hours Access
state_specifics: Keep an office with a working telephone, staffed during business hours (245.40(a)).
The office must protect record confidentiality and comply with fire-safety ordinances.
Adopt a written operating-hours policy telling clients how to reach the agency outside those hours.

policies.title: Liability Insurance and Employer Responsibilities
state_specifics: Keep evidence of liability insurance (245.90(a), 245.30(b)(2)). Submit proof with the initial application.
Policy minimums were not confirmed in the codified text. A secondary source says $1M per occurrence and $3M aggregate, so confirm with IDPH.
As a direct-service employer, the agency pays employment taxes, Social Security taxes and workers' compensation. State this in each client agreement.
Add hired and non-owned auto and employee-dishonesty (crime) coverage.

policies.title: Client Rights and Responsibilities
state_specifics: Annual worker training must cover client dignity, independence, self-determination, privacy, choice and rights (245.71(f)).
Give the rights and responsibilities statement to every client with the contract.
No one may be refused service based on the protected classes in 775 ILCS 5/1-103(Q).

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints (Complaint Resolution Policy)
state_specifics: Written complaint-resolution policy between the agency and its clients and client advocates is required (245.30(b)(3)). It is an initial-application document.
The client agreement must list contact information for concerns, complaints and questions (245.210(c)(6)).
Keep a complaint log with date received, investigation, resolution and response to the client.
Tell clients they may also contact IDPH. Read 245.115 in full before finalizing.

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: A written confidentiality policy must cover use, removal and release of client records (245.210(j)).
The office must protect record confidentiality (245.40(a)).
Keep personnel records confidential (245.30(c)(1)(G)).
HIPAA applies if the agency is a covered entity, for example through electronic Medicaid billing.

policies.title: Client Property, Gifts and Financial Exploitation Prevention
state_specifics: Financial exploitation is a reportable event under 245.250 and the Adult Protective Services Act (320 ILCS 20).
Employees may not borrow from, accept gifts from, or hold the credit cards or checks of clients.
Report suspected exploitation to the elder abuse provider agency designated by IDoA or the Area Agency on Aging.

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Language Access
state_specifics: No refusal of service on protected-class grounds (775 ILCS 5/1-103(Q); 245.210(d)).
Personnel policies must provide for compliance with the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (245.30(c)(1)(F)).
Provide interpreters or translated documents to clients with limited English proficiency, and communication aids for clients with disabilities, at no charge.

policies.title: Service Agreement, Rates and Billing Disclosure
state_specifics: The written client agreement must include (245.210(c)): Act and Background Check Act compliance; who pays taxes and workers' compensation; who supervises, hires, fires and disciplines; charges, payment schedule and payee; term and termination; complaint contact.
Attach the rights and responsibilities statement, service plan and rate sheet, and submit a copy of the current contract with the application.
Give the services list and scope of work for each service to the client before contracting, with the signed contract, and again whenever it changes (245.210(b)).
Text of 245.220 was not retrieved. Read it in full for added contract terms.

policies.title: Scope of Services — What Caregivers May and May Not Do
state_specifics: Home services are non-medical: ADL help, housekeeping, laundry, meal preparation, shopping, appointments and companionship (245.40(c); 245.210(a)). Nothing requiring a Nurse Practice Act licensee.
Keep a list of services offered and the scope of work for each, and submit the scope of services with the application.

Task limits (skin care, bathing, feeding, toileting and others) usually require client feedback, worker training and an agency competency evaluation. Some also need a health care professional's order (245.40(c)(4)).
No passive range of motion, no nail trimming, no skilled skin care, no medication setup.
The fetched text of 245.40(c)(4) stopped at item L. Read items M through P in full.

policies.title: Client Acceptance, Intake, Eligibility and Assessment
state_specifics: Written acceptance and discharge policies are required and must be followed (245.210(d)). It is an initial-application document.
Accept based on need for non-medical help, documented functional limitations, medications, treatments, activity, diet and mental status.
Do not provide medical services. Accept a totally dependent repositioning client only if the worker is trained and competency-evaluated and a representative can assist or give feedback.
No refusal on protected-class grounds.
Identify the client's payer and route Medicaid clients through CCP or DHS-DRS.

policies.title: Service Plan and Plan Updates
state_specifics: A written plan is required for every client, developed with the client or representative or POA, and family if the client wishes (245.210(e)). It is an initial-application sample form.
Contents: ADL and in-home support, medication reminders (frequency and time of day), treatments, activity, diet, functional limitations, mental status, visit frequency, equipment, client limitations.
No tasks outside the worker scope in 245.40(c)(4). No physician signature required.
Review and revise as needed, and at least annually.

policies.title: Supervisory Visits for Clients
state_specifics: Supervisory visits are required under 245.40(c)(6)(B). Written policy is an initial-application document.
The routine visit interval is not confirmed. A secondary source says 90 days, so read (c)(6)(B) in full before setting it.
When an area of concern is noted, an on-site visit is required within the next supervisory visit.
The designated supervisor must be available to workers for questions at all times.

policies.title: Supervisory Visits and Annual Observation of Home Services Workers
state_specifics: The supervisor makes an annual on-site visit to observe and assess each worker giving care (245.40(c)(6)).
Read subitems (B)(i) through (iii) in full for visit content. Written policy is an initial-application document.
Supervisors and trainers need at least 2 years of qualifying experience within the last 5 years, or meet the current-position-plus-training-within-one-year alternative (245.71(g)).
Document each visit and any follow-up.

policies.title: Medication Reminding and Self-Administration Support
state_specifics: Workers may only remind clients about medications pre-selected by the client, a family member, a nurse or a pharmacist and in containers other than prescription bottles, such as medication minders (245.40(c)(4)(N)).
Workers may not perform or provide medication setup (245.40(c)(5)(D)).
The service plan states reminder frequency and time of day.
Medication reminding is a required training topic (245.71(e)). Confirm exact subsection wording in the full text.

policies.title: Personal Care Task Limits, Positioning and Oxygen-Related Support
state_specifics: Tasks such as ambulation, bathing, dressing, feeding/thickener, positioning and toileting each have conditions in 245.40(c)(4).
Most require client or representative feedback, worker training in the method and an agency competency evaluation.
Some require a health care professional's order. Obtain it and file it in the client record.
Annual training must include oxygen delivery for workers who serve clients on oxygen (245.71(f)).

policies.title: Dementia Care and Related Training
state_specifics: Initial training must cover understanding dementia and problem-solving for challenging dementia behaviors, plus communicating with people with dementia (245.71(e)).
IDPH survey guidance cites 77 Ill. Adm. Code 973.140 for dementia training. Dementia training hours were not retrieved, so read 973.140 and 245.211 in full.
Document dementia training for every worker assigned to a dementia client.

policies.title: Scheduling, Missed Visits and Continuity of Care
state_specifics: Assign only workers who have passed the competency evaluation and completed background checks.
The operating-hours policy tells clients how to reach the agency after hours (245.40(a)).
No state missed-visit timeframe was found. Set the agency's own standard for notifying clients and arranging replacement coverage.
Match schedules to the visit frequency in the service plan.

policies.title: Electronic Visit Verification and Timekeeping
state_specifics: EVV applies to Medicaid-funded personal care. Illinois integrates data in HHAeXchange from March 2, 2026. HFS requires at least 75% quarterly EVV compliance from April 1, 2026.
The state EVV solution is offered free to providers.
Capture caregiver, client, service, time in, time out and GPS location.
Private-pay visits still need documentation of services at each visit (245.210(h)).

policies.title: Change in Client Condition and Emergencies in the Home
state_specifics: Workers observe, report and document changes in client functioning (245.40(c)).
Training must cover emergencies, first aid and the client's emergency preparedness plan (245.71(e)).
Call 911 for emergencies. Notify the representative and emergency contact in the record.
Report to the supervisor the same day.

policies.title: Discharge, Transfer and Discontinuation of Services
state_specifics: Written discharge policy required (245.210(d)).
Give at least 7 working days' written notice with a stated reason, and keep a copy in the record.
The 7-day notice does not apply when worker safety is at risk. Document the risk.
Document the plan for transfer or referral to another provider.

policies.title: Coordination with Medicaid Programs and Payers (CCP and HSP)
state_specifics: Programs serving exclusively through CCP, DHS-DRS or the VA are excluded from the licensing definition (245.20).
A licensee takes private pay or private insurance. Medicaid clients are served through IDoA CCP or DHS-DRS.
CCP in-home service S5130 is $30.80/hour, or $32.57 with insurance (eff. 1/1/2026). HSP homemaker (4100) is $30.80/hour (updated 7/1/2026).
IDoA is the waiver operating agency and HFS is the state Medicaid agency.
Confirm provider enrollment steps with IDoA and DRS before accepting Medicaid-funded clients.

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: Report reasonable suspicion of abuse, neglect or exploitation of a client 60+, a disabled client or any eligible adult to the elder abuse provider agency designated by IDoA or the Area Agency on Aging (245.250).
For a victim under 18, call the DCFS Child Abuse Hotline.
Document each report and keep it on premises for 12 months.
Employees and volunteers report to management and to the elder abuse provider agency or IDoA. Mandated-reporter duties under 320 ILCS 20 remain.

policies.title: Abuse Investigations and Law Enforcement Notification
state_specifics: If an employee is the alleged perpetrator, remove them from direct client contact immediately and investigate.
Complete a written investigation report within 14 days of the initial report. Send it to IDPH within 24 hours after the investigation is completed and keep a copy 12 months.
The report must contain the six elements in 245.250(d).
Call 911 or local police immediately for staff-inflicted physical injury, sexual abuse by staff, a crime in the home by another person, or a death other than by disease or natural causes.
A written law-enforcement notification policy is required.

policies.title: Incident Reporting
state_specifics: Workers observe, report and document incidents (245.71(e)).
Abuse, neglect or exploitation incidents follow 245.250 timelines.
Complete an incident report for falls, injuries, property loss, client elopement and worker injury, and review each in quality improvement.

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
state_specifics: Written policies and procedures for investigating, controlling and preventing infections (245.75(a)). It is an initial-application document.
Read 245.75(b), on CDC guidance, in full.
Training covers hygiene and infection control, initial and annual (245.71(e), (f)).
Influenza and pneumococcal vaccination rules (245.55) do not apply to home services agencies.

policies.title: Client Emergency and Disaster Plans
state_specifics: Initial training covers the client's emergency preparedness plan (245.71(e)).
Annual training must include disaster procedures (245.71(f)).
Record an emergency contact in each client record (245.210(h)).
Include an agency continuity plan covering office closure and caregiver coverage.

policies.title: Caregiver Safety in the Home and Workplace Violence
state_specifics: Written procedures for identifying potential dangers to personnel in the home and protecting them from those dangers (245.30(c)(1)(I)).
Assess the home at intake and at supervisory visits (hazards, pets, smoking, weapons, unsafe conditions).
Workers may leave an unsafe home and call the supervisor.
Safety precautions are a required training topic (245.71(e)).

policies.title: Transporting Clients
state_specifics: Transport to appointments is a permitted service (245.210(a)).
Verify a valid driver's license and auto insurance, and confirm hired and non-owned auto coverage.
Obtain written client consent. Follow the task limits for assisting with transfers.

policies.title: Caregiver Qualifications, Registry and Employment Conditions
state_specifics: For each worker not otherwise licensed, certified or registered, keep in the file (245.71(a)): no disqualifying background check without a waiver; Social Security card copy; visa or proof of citizenship.
For any position needing a State professional license, verify with IDFPR that it is active and keep a copy (245.30(c)(2)).
CNAs on the Health Care Worker Registry may have training accepted but still need the competency evaluation.

policies.title: Background Checks and Health Care Worker Registry
state_specifics: Comply with the Health Care Worker Background Check Act (225 ILCS 46) and Code 955 (245.72). Written process is an initial-application document.
Fingerprints go to the Illinois State Police within 10 working days (per the research). Results initiated through IDPH are entered in the Registry.
Proof of IDPH Registry access (955.115) is required in the application.
Annual Registry verification is a survey focus (IDPH guidance).
Read 955.145, 955.165 and 955.220 in full for process details.

policies.title: Orientation and Initial Training (10 Hours)
state_specifics: At least 10 hours of initial training per worker. Five hours before the first assignment, and 5 within 30 days of the start of employment (245.71(c)).
Proof of training from another licensed home services agency within the prior 365 days is acceptable, but the worker still gets a competency evaluation before the first assignment.

Required topics are listed in 245.71(e): job limits, communication, observation and reporting, personal care tasks, infection control, safety, emergencies, confidentiality, dementia, abuse and neglect reporting.
The 8-hour figure applies only to placement agencies.
Written employee training procedures are an initial-application document.

policies.title: Competency Evaluation Before First Assignment
state_specifics: No assignment until the worker passes a competency evaluation on the first 5 hours of topics.
A second evaluation follows the remaining 5 hours.
Task-specific competency evaluations apply for tasks under 245.40(c)(4).
Keep results in the personnel file.

policies.title: Annual Training and Annual Registry Verification
state_specifics: At least 10 hours per year of employment, on a calendar-year or anniversary basis chosen by the agency (245.71(f)). Initial 10 hours satisfy year one.
Self-study is allowed with demonstrated learning.
Required topics: client rights, disaster procedures, infection control, abuse and neglect reporting, ADL tasks in 245.40(c)(4)(A)-(P).
Verify each worker on the Health Care Worker Registry annually (IDPH guidance).

policies.title: Training Documentation and Trainer/Supervisor Qualifications
state_specifics: Document date, minutes per topic, instructor and qualifications, content description, and worker signature or electronic certificate with date/time stamp (245.71(i)).
Supervisors and trainers need 2 years of qualifying experience in the last 5 years, or a current position plus training within the past year.
Supervisors and trainers must be available to workers for continuing education.

policies.title: Initial Employee Health Evaluation and TB Screening
state_specifics: Each new employee with client contact needs an initial health evaluation as specified by the governing body (245.30(c)(1)(B)).
The rule does not state a specific TB test. The governing body sets the requirement in writing.
Keep results confidential and apart from the personnel file.

policies.title: Employee Health and Safety Policy — Illness and Exposure Reporting
state_specifics: Employees must report health symptoms and exposure to communicable or infectious disease, and the policy states when they are removed from and may resume client contact (245.30(c)(1)(H)).
245.90(a)(3)(I)(ii) cites both (H) and (I) for the employee health and safety policy. Submit it with the initial application.
Link to infection control (245.75) and caregiver safety procedures.

policies.title: Personnel Policies: Wage Scales, Benefits, Hours and Leave
state_specifics: Written policies on wage scales, benefits, hours of work and leave time must be available to all full- and part-time employees (245.30(c)(1)(A)).
Paid leave under the Illinois Paid Leave for All Workers Act accrues at least 2.5% of hours worked. Confirm local ordinances, including Chicago.
Minimum wage law is 820 ILCS 105. Confirm the current state, Cook County and Chicago rates.

policies.title: Job Descriptions for All Positions
state_specifics: Job descriptions are required for all positions the agency uses (245.30(c)(1)(D)). Submit them with the initial application.
Include agency manager, alternate manager, supervisor, scheduler and caregiver.
The caregiver description must match the 245.40(c) scope and exclude nursing tasks.

policies.title: Personnel Records
state_specifics: Each file holds name and address, SSN, date of birth, next of kin, evidence of qualifications, employment dates and reason for separation (245.30(c)(3)).
Also keep the Social Security card copy, proof of work authorization, background check results, training and competency records.
Keep personnel records confidential (245.30(c)(1)(G)).
The manager keeps personnel files (245.40(a)).

policies.title: Annual Performance Evaluation
state_specifics: Annual performance evaluation of each employee (245.30(c)(1)(E)).
Combine with the annual observation of each worker required by 245.40(c)(6) and with annual training review.

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: Prohibit gifts, loans, personal financial dealings and relationships that exploit a client.
Employees are mandated to report suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation (245.250).
Alleged perpetrators are removed from client contact pending investigation.

policies.title: Contracted Staff and Third-Party Providers
state_specifics: Contracted workers must hold any required license, registration or certification and be supervised by the agency (245.30(c)(5)).

Third-party contracts must be written and cover services, adherence to agency policies and personnel requirements, agency control, notes, charges, liability and insurance, term, signatures and termination (245.210(b)).
Contracted workers meet the same background check and training standards.

policies.title: Wage, Hour and Overtime Compliance
state_specifics: Home care workers employed by the agency are covered by FLSA minimum wage and overtime rules (29 CFR 552).
Pay for travel time between clients and for required training and orientation.
State, Cook County and Chicago minimum wage rates were from secondary sources and conflict for Chicago. Confirm with IDOL and the City of Chicago, and re-check every July 1 and January 1.
The client agreement states who is the employer and who pays taxes and workers' compensation (245.210(c)).

policies.title: Client Records Content and Retention
state_specifics: Each record holds identifying information, representative contact, emergency contact, agreed service plan, signed home care services agreement and worker documentation of each service at each visit (245.210(h)).
Written records policy required. It is an initial-application document.
Retain at least 2 years after the last date of service, in hard copy or electronic form.
Faxed copies must be on non-thermal paper.

policies.title: Client Records Management, Use and Release
state_specifics: Written confidentiality policy covers use, removal and release of records (245.210(j)).
Release records only with written client or representative authorization unless the law requires otherwise.
Store records so the office protects their confidentiality (245.40(a)).

policies.title: Required Reports to the State
state_specifics: Send the written abuse/neglect/exploitation investigation report to IDPH within 24 hours after the investigation is completed (245.250).
Notify IDPH within 10 days of any change (Facility Information Change Form).
Get approval before entering a new county.
Renewal is due before the full license expires. Form 445104 says 60 days before.

policies.title: Caregiver Visit Documentation
state_specifics: Workers document services at each visit (245.40(c); client record definition in 245.20).
Visit notes go into the client record and support billing.
Supervisors review notes at supervisory visits.

documents.title: Home Services Application (initial, renewal and change of ownership). The page titled "Required documentation to be provided with this application" lists the initial-applicant policy checklist.
documents.issuer: Illinois Department of Public Health, Health Care Facilities and Programs Section
documents.version: The form footer reads 'Updated 8/9/2023' on pp. 1-5 and 'Updated 6/8/2023' on pp. 6-8. The file posted on the IDPH site is named hs-application-092024.pdf.
documents.how_used: This is the main document. No single policy-review checklist exists apart from the application, so the 'Initial Applicants ONLY' checklist on page 8 is the item list, with the document's own regulatory cites as item IDs. Application-only items are excluded: forms, ownership, governing-body officers, revenue sources, client counts, geographic area, employee roster, manager qualification form (Attachment E), affidavits, fee, proof of liability coverage (245.90 a) 2)) and proof of Health Care Worker Registry access (955.115).

documents.title: Home Health, Home Services, and Home Nursing Agency Code, 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245 (Sections 245.30, 245.40, 245.90 and 245.210)
documents.issuer: Illinois Department of Public Health (published by JCAR)
documents.version: Current codified text on the ILGA/JCAR site. Section 245.30(c) shown here is the version cited in the search results (Section 245.40 history notes an amendment effective Nov. 8, 2023).
documents.how_used: This supports the application checklist. <cite index="33-4">Section 245.90(a)(3)(I) requires copies of policies and procedures with the initial application, starting with complaint resolution (245.30(b)(3)) and employee health and safety (245.30(c)(1)(H) and (I)).</cite> <cite index="33-5,33-7,33-8">It also requires client service contracts (245.220), acceptance criteria (245.210(d)) and sample service plan forms (245.210(e)).</cite> I could not open the full regulation text directly; the ilga.gov pages returned permission errors. The wording of regulation items below comes from search excerpts.

documents.title: Surveillance Nurse Visit Checklist (Home Services)
documents.how_used: Used only to show how the policy manual is reviewed at survey. It lists policy and procedure manuals, bylaws, governing body minutes, complaint log and process, training files, job descriptions, service plan, and Alzheimer's/dementia training curriculum. These are not added as required policy items.

required_items.text: A copy of the current client contract per 245.220 for Home Services, plus any attachments noted in the contract (e.g., rights and responsibilities, service plan, rate sheet).
A copy of your scope of services.
Initial applicants only: copy of job description for all positions.
Initial applicants only: complaint resolution policy.
Initial applicants only: employee health and safety policy. Section 245.90(a)(3)(I)(ii) cites both 245.30(c)(1)(H) and (I) for this policy.
Initial applicants only: infection control policy.
Initial applicants only: health care worker background check process.
Initial applicants only: supervisory visit for client policy.
Initial applicants only: supervisory visit for home service worker policy.
required_items.cite: IDPH Form 445104, p. 8 (245.40 c) 6 B i - iii))

required_items.text: Initial applicants only: client records management and release requirements.
Initial applicants only: employee training procedures.
Initial applicants only: acceptance of client policy. <cite index="16-5">The regulation says home services agencies shall develop and follow policies on acceptance and discharge of clients.</cite>
Initial applicants only: sample service plan form.

Personnel policies, available to all full- and part-time employees: wage scales, benefits, hours of work and leave time. These are regulation content not listed separately on the application checklist.
Personnel policies: requirements for an initial health evaluation of each new employee (or placed worker) who has contact with clients, as specified by the governing body.
Personnel policies: orientation to the agency and appropriate continuing education.
Personnel policies: job descriptions for all positions used by the agency.

Personnel policies: employee health policies requiring employees to report health symptoms and exposure to communicable or infectious disease, and specifying when employees are removed from and may resume client contact.
Personnel policies: agency procedures for identifying potential dangers to the health and safety of personnel providing services in the home, and for protecting them from those dangers.

sections: Required documentation (all applicants): client contract per 245.220 with attachments; scope of services; fee schedule

Initial Applicants ONLY: job descriptions; proof of liability coverage; complaint resolution policy; employee health and safety policy; infection control policy; health care worker background check process; supervisory visit for client policy; supervisory visit for home service worker policy; client records management and release; employee training procedures; acceptance of client policy; sample service plan form; proof of Health Care Worker Registry access

official.notes: The application has no numbered items. It uses a bulleted checklist, and each line carries a regulatory cite in parentheses, which I used as the item ID. The policies are due with an initial application, mailed to IDPH with the $1,500 fee (the form says electronic submission is not accepted). The checklist does not require the manual to follow any set order or category scheme, so mirroring the checklist order is a sensible way to organize it. IDPH surveyors later ask to see the 'Policy and Procedure Manuals' (surveillance checklist). I left out these checklist lines as non-policy paperwork: proof of general liability coverage ($1M per occurrence / $3M aggregate, 245.90(a)(2)), proof of Health Care Worker Registry access (955.115), and the Attachment E manager qualification form. The fee schedule is also not listed as a policy item. Gaps: (1) The full text of 245.30(c)(1)(E)-(G), 245.40(c) and 245.210(e)-(h) was not retrievable in full, so I did not list items I could not confirm. Check the full Part 245 text on the JCAR site for those. (2) The application's checklist cites only 245.30(c)(1)(I) for employee health and safety, while 245.90(a)(3)(I)(ii) cites both (H) and (I), so cover both. (3) For Alzheimer's/dementia training, see 245.211 and 77 Ill. Adm. Code 973, which the surveillance checklist asks for. This is a training curriculum, not a policy checklist item. (4) Agencies serving only CCP, DHS-DRS or VA clients may be excluded from IDPH licensure (245.20), and the application's client counts exclude those clients.
